name: react: a standing reaction fires on genuine change, not on seed or unchanged writes
description: A node declares edges.react = [{ when: 'counter.n', run: [derive counter.doubled = counter.n * 2] }]. The reaction baseline is seeded from the pre-event snapshot, so it does NOT fire on init; it fires only when its `when` value actually changes. Step 1 changes n (0 -> 5) and the reaction fires, so one patch carries both the assign and the derived double. Step 2 writes the SAME n (5): the assign op is still emitted, but the reaction does not fire (when unchanged). Step 3 changes n again (5 -> 7) and the reaction fires once more. Proves reactions are change-triggered, once-per-change, and settle inside the same dispatch/rev.
